title: Which of these rectangles have the same shape?
description: Four rectangles with measured sides are compared two at a time. The video divides each new side by the old side to get a factor for the width and one for the height, then multiplies back to check.
teaching_notes: One idea: two rectangles have the same shape when the width and the height change by the same factor. Watch for students who judge by the look of the rectangles or by their size alone.

source: Figure it Out (ratios and proportions, question 4)
video_script.why: The child must decide sameness of shape from measures and not by eye, using the same factor test as the tiger pictures.
video_script.substitution: Divide the new width by the old width and the new height by the old height, and compare the two factors.
video_script.anchor: four rectangles K, L, M and N, each with its width and height measured with a scale
video_script.payoff_line: Rectangles K and M are similar, and so are L and N.

final_answer.value: K and M are similar, and L and N are similar
final_answer.spoken: rectangles K and M are similar, and rectangles L and N are similar

hold_back: Answer: K and M are similar
maths_rules: sample measures used to show the method (the book's figure has no stated scale): K is 2 cm by 6 cm, L is 3 cm by 2 cm, M is 3 cm by 9 cm, N is 6 cm by 4 cm
L to N: 6 ÷ 3 = 2 and 4 ÷ 2 = 2; the same factor 2, so L and N are similar
K to M: 3 ÷ 2 = 3/2 and 9 ÷ 6 = 3/2; the same factor 3/2, so K and M are similar
K to L: 3 ÷ 2 = 3/2 and 2 ÷ 6 = 1/3; different factors, so K and L are not similar
video_script.design: One idea: the same factor on width and height means the same shape. Uses the factor of change from the solved example. The four rectangles stay for the whole video.
open_questions: The book's figure of five rectangles has no stated scale, so the video shows the method on four sample rectangles with sample measures. The child then measures the book's own rectangles.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about rectangles.
<bookmark mark='rects'/>Four rectangles lie side by side, and each one is measured with a scale.
<bookmark mark='scale'/>K is two by six, and L is three by two. M is three by nine, and N is six by four.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which of these rectangles have the same shape as each other?

beats.on_screen: the four rectangles hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: two rectangles with an arrow from the old width to the new width and another from the old height to the new height, each marked new ÷ old; the word similar is written under them

marks.name: the word similar is written under two rectangles of the same shape
marks.method: two arrows marked new ÷ old join the old sides to the new sides
marks.div: the words new width ÷ old width and new height ÷ old height are written beside the arrows

narration: <bookmark mark='name'/>Rectangles with the same shape are called similar.
<bookmark mark='method'/>We test two rectangles the same way as the example in your book.
<bookmark mark='div'/>Divide the new width by the old width, and the new height by the old height.
<bookmark mark='same'/>If both factors are the same, the rectangles are similar.

beats.on_screen: Given: K 2 × 6, L 3 × 2, M 3 × 9, N 6 × 4 (width × height, in cm)

marks.given: the four measures are written one under the other

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, in centimetres, K is two by six, and L is three by two. M is three by nine, and N is six by four.

beats.on_screen: To find: the rectangles with equal width factor and height factor

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the rectangles whose sides change by the same factor.

beats.on_screen: L to N: width factor 6 ÷ 3 = 2; height factor 4 ÷ 2 = 2; the same

marks.qs: the heading L to N is written
marks.h: the height factor 4 ÷ 2 = 2 is written under it
marks.same: a tick lands between the two factors

narration: <bookmark mark='qs'/>Step one, go from L to N and divide each new side by the old side.
<bookmark mark='w'/>Six divided by three is two.
<bookmark mark='h'/>Four divided by two is also two.
<bookmark mark='same'/>The factors are the same, so L and N are similar.

beats.on_screen: K to M: width factor 3 ÷ 2 = 3/2; height factor 9 ÷ 6 = 3/2; the same

marks.pr: the heading K to M is written
marks.h: the height factor 9 ÷ 6 = 3/2 is written under it
marks.same: a tick lands between the two factors

narration: <bookmark mark='pr'/>Step two, go from K to M in the same way.
<bookmark mark='w'/>Three divided by two is three halves.
<bookmark mark='h'/>Nine divided by six is also three halves.
<bookmark mark='same'/>The factors are the same, so K and M are similar.

beats.on_screen: K to L: width factor 3 ÷ 2 = 3/2; height factor 2 ÷ 6 = 1/3; different

marks.pq: the heading K to L is written
marks.h: the height factor 2 ÷ 6 = 1/3 is written under it
marks.diff: the two factors show in the warning colour

narration: <bookmark mark='pq'/>Step three, see whether the two pairs join up by going from K to L.
<bookmark mark='w'/>Three divided by two is three halves.
<bookmark mark='h'/>Two divided by six is one third.
<bookmark mark='diff'/>The factors are different, so the two pairs are separate.

marks.chk: the words Check: put the factors back are written

narration: <bookmark mark='chk'/>Step four, put the factors back to check.
<bookmark mark='q'/>Three times two is six, and two times two is four. These are the sides of N.
<bookmark mark='p'/>Two times three halves is three, and six times three halves is nine. These are the sides of M.

beats.on_screen: Answer: K and M are similar; L and N are similar
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Rectangles K and M are similar, and so are L and N.
